faq.a1: By counting the net deposit performance of agents, sales or businesses, corresponding rewards or rebates are automatically issued to encourage new recruits and capital growth behaviors.
faq.a2: The net deposit reward is based on "deposit minus withdrawal" to calculate the net fund inflow performance. It does not rely on transaction volume or customer order data, and is more focused on fund contribution incentives.
faq.a3:
The system will automatically perform statistics and reward calculations for the previous cycle on the 1st of each month. The length of the cycle is determined by the configuration item "Number of Statistics Months" (optional from 1 to 12 months). 
For example: If the period is 3 months, the statistics for October 1, 2025 will be the data for July, August, and September.
faq.a4: If the average net deposit (reward) ≤ 0, the user has no reward record this month and the system will automatically skip the calculation.
faq.a5: Administrators can multiple-select the following account types in the configuration: ● User (end customer) ● Agent (IB) ● Sales ● Business. Only the selected types will be included in statistics and reward execution.
faq.q1: What is the core goal of the net deposit bonus feature?
faq.q2: What is the difference between net deposit bonus and regular commission?
faq.q3:
On which day is the reward calculation performed? 
Automatic?
faq.q4: What will happen to users whose net deposit ≤ 0?
faq.q5: What types of reward objects are supported?

moreFaq.a1:
● CRM deposit: from orders that have passed the deposit review (excluding handling fees, converted to USD based on the exchange rate).

● System deposit: from the operation type selected in the system fund operation record.

● The exchange rate calculation uses the central parity rate = (buying price selling price) / 2.
moreFaq.a10:
● Automatic review is turned on → rewards are credited directly to your account;

● Turn off automatic review → the reward will enter "pending review" and the administrator will manually operate it in the reward review list.
moreFaq.a11:
● Average net deposit (reward) ≤ 0

● Reward parameter ≤ 0

● Reward parameter difference ≤ 0

● The user does not have a collection account and automatic review is not enabled.
moreFaq.a12: Administrators can check whether the statistical results are empty in the "Net Deposit Data Statistics Table"; if abnormal, they can re-trigger the statistical task or contact the technical team to perform manual recalculation.
moreFaq.a2:
Net deposit = total deposit − total withdrawal. 
The statistical period is the number of natural months set in the configuration item (such as 3 months)
moreFaq.a3:
Personal average net deposit: only calculate the user's personal average net deposit.

Average net deposit (reward) = Calculate the average net deposit of "own direct subordinates (users)"

Graded average net deposit: Calculate the average net deposit of "all your subordinates" and use it to determine reward parameters based on the graded reward table.
moreFaq.a4: The system will look for the tiered reward parameter table range corresponding to the account type based on each user's "tiered average net deposit" and automatically match the corresponding percentage (%).
moreFaq.a5: If the administrator sets "fixed parameters" for a user in the configuration, the system ignores the grading table and directly uses the fixed parameters to calculate rewards.
moreFaq.a6:
By default, data statistics and calculations in the previous cycle (1-12 months defined by the configuration item) are executed on the 1st of each month. 
For example: If the period is 3 months, the statistics for October 1, 2025 will be the data for July, August, and September.
moreFaq.a7:
① First calculate the individual average net deposit and the graded average net deposit.

② Then match the reward parameters.

③ Implement personal rewards.

④ Then implement the graded difference rewards step by step upwards (that is, the superior will get the graded difference rebate).

⑤ Determine whether to automatically review and issue according to configuration.
moreFaq.a8:
● Personal reward = average net deposit (reward) × reward parameter

● Level difference reward = average net deposit (lower level) × (upper level parameter − lower level parameter)

commissionRebateSettings.agentEditDesc: Agents can edit the commission parameters of direct subordinates on the user terminal.
commissionRebateSettings.commissionGroupNameTips:
Level: The level of this level = the level of the lower level.

Leap level: the level of this level > the level of the lower level.

No commission rebate: When a level is leveled or skipped, the level will not receive commission rebate.

Fixed commission: When there is a leveling or skipping level, the level will receive a fixed commission.

Obtain commission % from subordinates: When there is a level or skip level, the commission obtained by this level is the percentage of the commission obtained by the direct subordinate, and the commission obtained by the subordinate will not be affected.

faq.a1:
The total rebate value refers to the upper limit of the cumulative rebate amount that can be obtained by all agents in a complete agency chain. 
The total rebate value for each agent line is fixed and cannot be exceeded.
faq.a2:
Please click the Agent Edit button to open the customer relationship graph:

1. First set the total rebate value of the agent line

2. Then fill in the rebate parameters of each agent by level, and fill in different commission parameters according to different commission parameter methods.
faq.a3: There are two ways to set rebate custom parameters: 1.Basic method 2.Grade method. You can choose which method to use to calculate specific rebate parameters.
faq.a4:
Basic method fills in the user's specific rebate parameter value. When rebate is given to the corresponding agent user according to the filled in rebate parameters (how much is returned), the lowest-level agent does not need to fill in the rebate parameters, but uses the total rebate value - the total rebate of the upper-level agent.

Note: The total rebate amount shall not exceed the total rebate value.
faq.a5:
Fill in the rebate parameters of each level of agents in the level difference method. When rebates are made, the rebate parameters of the hit agent will be filled in. The rebate level difference of the upper-level agent (upper-level agent parameters - lower-level agent parameters) is filled in. When filling in, the rebate parameters of the top agent A1 (the first level of customer relationship) are the total rebate value. 
The rebate parameter of the subordinate agent B1 must be less than or equal to the rebate parameter value of the upper-level agent, and so on. 
The rebate parameter value of each agent shall not be greater than the rebate parameter value of the superior agent;

=Remarks: (1) The parameter allows up to two decimal places (2) must be a positive number
faq.a6:
Won't. 
The adjustment of rebate parameters will only affect the trading behavior after the setting takes effect, and historical transactions will not be affected.
